system.summary: Invented-sign simple substitution for French with a few homophones (a, e, l, u), nulls between doubled letters, and at least one name code.
system.notes: Tomokiyo's table plus: slash = c as well as l; the c and d hooks interchange; z also t; X = m and u; a null (p+omega, vf, small S, dots) is written between doubled letters; the 1535 letter uses a Latin R for o and beta for v. The name code '/ X y X / X' is glossed 'Rang..' (Guido Rangone).

prior_solution.where: Key table only: S. Tomokiyo, cryptiana francis.htm 'Selve's Cipher' (reconstructed from fr. 3045 ff. 42-49; names fr. 3091 f. 25 as the same cipher); no plaintext published. Contemporary partial decipherments on the leaves (glosses). DECODE 'Non-decrypted'. Charriere, Negociations dans le Levant I, prints other Selve letters of 1535-36, not these.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue card (item 178). No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE R3697/R4232 metadata (R3697 is fr. 3091 f. 25, not fr. 3045); Tomokiyo francis.htm gives the key table for Selve's cipher, no plaintext; BnF catalogue records cite no edition.
Gallica btv1b9060156p views 82-95 (fr. 3045) and btv1b9060253s views 27-28 (fr. 3091) at 2600-4400 px and native; cipher located on views 84, 85, 86, 88, 94 and on f. 25r-v.
Tomokiyo's table applied to fr. 3045 view 84 line 1: 'en tres grand danger combien que le nombre des assiegeans'.
One agent per page on R4232 (views 84, 85, 86/88/94): 1448 signs, extra homophones and the doubling nulls found; four glossed runs agree with the readings.
R4232 open spots re-read on native crops: v94 'ceste annee' (the unread verb), v88 'guerre'; name code valued from its gloss 'Rang..'.
Charriere, Negociations de la France dans le Levant I, pp. 265-320 read page by page on Gallica (no OCR): Selve letters of 18 June 1535, 22 Aug 1535, 24 Jan and 8 Feb 1536 printed, not these two.
R3697 first pass (f. 25r, f. 25v): about 70% / 50% of the unstruck cipher; new signs R = o, beta = v; soft film scan.
DECODE images of R3697 fetched with the project cookie: screenshots of the same film at lower resolution; no gain.
R3697 second pass with the extended table: f. 25r 92%, f. 25v lower block 97% of the unstruck cipher.

R3697 third pass: the decipherer's glosses used as cribs on the struck runs ('au marchant', 'ung sansacque cy prochain', 'amiablement pour la charge qu'il a de Vesprim'); struck runs from about 20% to 40%; 'soubz umbre de marchandise', 'fus adverty, meu de coniecture' read.
f. 25r r8-r9 read as '... Anthon[e] de Le[yve] de luy tenir le guet' (Antonio de Leyva, governor of Milan); not secured by the signs.
fr. 3019 f. 97r (Rodez and Selve, 16 Nov 1536) opened: three short glossed runs in the same cipher; no occurrence of the open r8 name.
5 Oct 2026: Gallica checked again for a newer (colour) digitisation of fr. 3091: only the film scan btv1b9060253s (105 views). Native views 27/28 re-fetched (8699x5866, 9037x5865 grey).

5 Oct 2026: struck runs re-transcribed at native resolution, 1.6-2x crops: f. 25v T1 (x 2350-4150, y 1080-1230) and f. 25r C2 middle (x 5250-7900, y 4740-4900). The strike sits on the x-height of every sign; only the shapes already recorded (ses amis, et gran, avoit, amiablement, luy) separate; the rest are joined blobs. No new sign secured.

5 Oct 2026: strike removal by a fitted strike line with vertical interpolation (img/destrike.py) on f. 25r C2: the fitted band also removes the sign bodies (they share the x-height); nothing new legible.

5 Oct 2026: C2 middle signs (W ɦ ‡ ot ω ot x z q ꝏ ot ‡ / ꝏ ʒ 7 ‡ ot ꝏ L 4 p / / ω ot) tested against gloss-led candidates (de ses maistres, grand credit, du Turc); none fits the recorded shapes; r8 'a pr[...]' retested with ∂ = a and ∂ɜ = r (a paie / a prevenu / a prié): no fit.

5 Oct 2026: the old measure (stats.py) counts every sign with a key value, sense or not. New sense.py counts only signs inside French words (fr-1520s-diplomatic vocabulary + named persons/places) by best-coverage segmentation, runs under 4 letters not counted: R4232 98.5%, R3697 78.2%, both 89.9% (2230/2481), against 90.6% by signs.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R3697_signs.txt / R4232_signs.txt with READING_R3697.md / READING_R4232.md; key KEY.md (Tomokiyo's table with the additions)

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): READING_R4232.md and READING_R3697.md read through. R4232 reads as continuous French (reviewed A); R3697's unstruck cipher reads with scattered holes (reviewed B); the decipherer's struck runs (304 signs) give only fragments and are split off as decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.899 -> 0.877 (signs in text that reads).

Re-read of the R3697 struck runs under REREAD_BRIEF (batch mix1): the decipherer’s glosses taken as the contemporary decipherment they are; C1 gloss re-read on native_f27.jpg (one blurred group left); the glossed runs A, B, C1 + C2 head, T2 (169 signs) set out as text and checked against the pass-3 sign alignments, split off as read (READING_R3697_struck.md, R3697_struck_en.md); C2 tail, C3, T1, T3 (135 signs) stay decoded, not read (no legible gloss, strike over every sign).

texts.label: R3697, BnF fr. 3091 f. 25r-v, Venice, 14 Sept 1535: unstruck cipher (f. 25r r03-r16, f. 25v L1-L5)
texts.summary: Georges de Selve, ambassador at Venice, to Francis I: a merchant must go to France by the Swiss road because the Imperial ambassador at Venice suspects him and has had the other road watched; that ambassador had urged him to go to the French court under colour of trade; on the verso a Hungarian matter (Hieronymus, Veszprém) and informants reporting to the Turk. The runs struck through by the King's decipherer are read only in part.

reading_review.note: The unstruck cipher of R3697 (747 signs) reads as French sentences: the merchant must take the Swiss road; the Emperor's ambassador had him watched and had urged him to go to the French court under colour of trade; certain persons kept advising the Turk. Holes: a blot and a cancelled name (Anthon[e] de Le...), a few isolated signs. Audit grade C refined: the fragments are the struck runs, split off as decoded, not read.

texts.label: R3697, BnF fr. 3091 f. 25r-v: the struck runs with no legible gloss (C2 after "et gran[d]", C3, T1, T3; 135 signs)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (R3697_struck_reread_log.md): the glossed struck runs were split off and read from the decipherer’s glosses; these 135 signs have no gloss, or a gloss that is illegible where they need it (f. 25v margin lines 1-2, 6-7), and the strike crosses the x-height of every sign on the only (film) image. Fragments only: "avoit", "on fait ... contre ses", "-tretienent". Blocker: illegible; a colour or multispectral image, or the original, would separate the lighter strike ink.

texts.label: R4232, BnF fr. 3045 ff. 42-49, Venice, 5 July 1536
texts.summary: Selve to Francis I on the Emperor's plan against Marseille (key to the kingdom; master of Provence, a land road Italy-Spain, the Mediterranean; the French galleys trapped in the port under the guns of La Garde), de Vaulx's advice to send the fleet towards Naples, La Forest's news from the Porte of an open breach with the Emperor, and the Pope's refusal of tenths to Charles. Four runs glossed by the King's decipherer agree with the reading.

reading_review.note: READING_R4232.md reads as continuous French (the Emperor's design on Marseille, the galleys, the delay, the breach with the Emperor) with a few single-sign holes; the margin decipherment of f. 44v agrees word for word.

texts.label: R3697, BnF fr. 3091 f. 25r-v: the struck runs glossed by the King’s decipherer (f. 25r A, B, C1 with the head of C2; f. 25v T2)
texts.summary: Read from the decipherer’s interlinear and marginal glosses, checked against the struck signs where they separate from the strike: "au marchant"; "ung sansacque cy prochain"; "Il a consumé ses facultez et la plus part de ses amys [...] et grand du T[urc]"; "amiablement pour la charge qu’il a de Vesprim de la guerre en luy".

reading_review.note: READING_R3697_struck.md: the four glossed runs (169 signs) read as French clauses from the contemporary glosses; signs agree where visible (A 11/11, B prochain 8/8, C2 head by the key, T2 about 50 of 64); C1 rests on the gloss alone (the strike hides its signs); one blurred group in the C1 gloss stays a hole. Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026: every word of the four runs is carried by the glosses (A, B, C1) or the margin decipherment and the signs (T2); 0 words bracketed, 0 replaced. Scored on the reading body (the four runs): 0.25 clean sentences, below the 0.60 rule.

texts.note: Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026: the four glossed runs are clause fragments set in clear text (A two words, B and T2 without their clause, C1 with a hole after "amys"); 0.25 clean sentences on the reading body, below the 0.60 rule, so decoded, not read; READING_R3697_struck.md is kept as a partial reading. Blocker: the rest of each clause is under the decipherer's strike (C1 after "amys", the tail of B, the head of T1) and illegible on the film scan.
